security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by JavaScript template literals and Markdown inline code. The remaining confirmed findings are expected network fetches and documented Node or npm commands used for Expo workflow validation. No prompt injection, credential harvesting, data exfiltration, or destructive behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict fetch.js to documented Expo and GitHub raw URLs, or require explicit user confirmation before fetching other hosts.
Add a scripts package manifest and lockfile before recommending npm install, and require confirmation before installing dependencies.
Keep command usage limited to the bundled Node scripts and avoid passing unreviewed URLs or unexpected workflow paths.

content.value_statement: Expo teams need workflow files that match current EAS syntax and schema rules. This skill helps create, edit, and validate EAS workflow YAML with official references.
actual_capabilities: Fetches the current official EAS workflow schema for workflow guidance.
Creates and edits workflow YAML files under .eas/workflows.
Validates workflow files against the official schema with a Node validator.
Explains triggers, jobs, runner options, expressions, and workflow structure.
Checks job references, dependencies, expressions, and required fields.
limitations: Requires network access to fetch current Expo schema and documentation.
Does not deploy apps or run EAS builds by itself.
Validation depends on the availability of the Expo schema endpoint.
May require installing Node dependencies for the validator.

use_cases.title: Create a Release Workflow
use_cases.description: Generate an EAS workflow that builds and submits an Expo app for production release.

use_cases.title: Debug Validation Errors
use_cases.description: Review an existing workflow and fix schema, trigger, dependency, or expression issues.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Automation
use_cases.description: Create consistent workflow patterns for previews, internal builds, and production deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new workflow file
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Expo EAS workflow that runs on pull requests and builds a preview version. Use the current schema.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Existing YAML
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of a workflow file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my preview workflow, validate it against the current EAS schema, and explain the fixes needed.

prompt_templates.title: Add Release Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Update my EAS workflow to build iOS and Android, submit to stores, and keep job dependencies clear.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Environment Pipelines
prompt_templates.prompt: Design EAS workflows for preview, staging, and production with manual inputs, concurrency controls, and reusable defaults.

output_examples.input: Create a workflow for preview builds on pull requests.
output_examples.output: A schema-aligned workflow plan with pull request triggers, preview build jobs, required parameters, and validation notes.

output_examples.input: Why does my workflow fail validation?
output_examples.output: A concise review that identifies invalid fields, missing values, broken dependencies, and recommended corrections.

output_examples.input: List available EAS workflow job types.
output_examples.output: A current summary from the fetched Expo schema, with job purposes and important parameters.

best_practices: Fetch the current Expo workflow schema before creating or changing workflows.
Validate every edited workflow before considering the CI/CD change complete.
Keep job names, dependencies, and expressions simple for teammate review.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on memorized EAS job names or outdated examples.
Do not skip validation after editing workflow YAML.
Do not hardcode secrets directly in workflow files.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create, edit, explain, and validate Expo EAS workflow YAML files.

faq.question: Does it use the latest EAS workflow syntax?
faq.answer: It is designed to fetch the current official schema and documentation first.

faq.question: Can it run builds or submit apps?
faq.answer: No. It helps define workflow files, but EAS runs the build and submit jobs.

faq.question: Why does it need network access?
faq.answer: It fetches official Expo schema and documentation so workflows use current options.

faq.question: Why does it include scripts?
faq.answer: The scripts fetch reference data with caching and validate workflow YAML.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
